notes.1: By design: a hyphen is reserved for the names of Psalm itself, an unknown name with a hyphen is rejected.
notes.2: The type is read as `static`, and `@return $this` alone is also marked as returning the object itself, as the documentation describes.
notes.3: Bug: `$this` is read as `static`, any instance of the called class, although the documentation tells them apart: "`@return static` is not enough: the method may return another instance of the class". Only `@return $this` alone keeps the object.

notes.1: By design: `&` and `|` are not mixed without parentheses, phpstan#1877.
notes.2: By design: `?` is not combined with `|` or `&`, as in native PHP types, phpdoc-parser#321.
notes.3: Differs: Psalm reads `?(A&B)`, TypeLang reads `(?A)&B`, which is `A&B`. Neither reading is documented, PHPStan requires parentheses.
notes.4: Bug: `B` is lost, `A|null` is returned instead of `(A&B)|null`.
notes.5: Bug: `B` is lost and `A&C` is returned, while `A&(B&C)` gives `A&B&C`.
notes.6: By design: the arrays of a union are merged into `array`, which also admits a mixed array `[A, B]`, for the projects that wrote `int[]|string[]` meaning either, psalm#5212.
notes.7: Bug: `?B` is lost and `A[]` is returned, `(A|?B)` alone gives `A`.

notes.1: By design: the type of every parameter and the return type are required, as the PHPStan documentation says.
notes.2: Not implemented: only the postfix form `int...` is read, phpdoc-parser#125.
notes.3: Not implemented: `...` needs a type or a name after it.
notes.4: Not implemented: a parameter of a callable needs a type.
notes.5: Bug: the `&` is dropped and the parameter is read as passed by value, as in psalm#14874.
notes.6: Not implemented: only the bare optional marker `=` is read, not a default value.
notes.7: Bug: `$this` is read as `static`, any instance of the called class, although the documentation tells them apart: "`@return static` is not enough: the method may return another instance of the class". Only `@return $this` alone keeps the object.
notes.8: Not implemented: a conditional type is read only inside parentheses.
notes.9: By design: a conditional type is read only in parentheses, as the documentation says.
notes.10: Not implemented: a parameter list is read only after `callable`, `Closure` and their variants.
notes.11: Not implemented: in a docblock a space at the top level ends the type, except around `|` and `&` and before `{` and `:`, and the rest becomes the description. Such exceptions are added on request, psalm#10000.
notes.12: Differs: Psalm takes `T&U` as the return type, PHPStan and TypeLang read `(callable(): T)&U`. Neither reading is documented, Psalm itself ends the return type at `|`.
notes.13: Bug: `?T|U` is taken as the return type, while `callable(): T|U` is read as `(callable(): T)|U`.
notes.14: Not implemented: a callable as a return type is read only inside parentheses, `callable(): (callable(): T)`.
notes.15: Bug: Psalm reads `callable(): ((callable(): T)|U)`, the `|` leaves only the inner callable, while `callable(): T|U` is read as `(callable(): T)|U`.

notes.1: By design: named and positional keys are not mixed, a dedicated error says so.

notes.4: Not implemented: the sign belongs to the number token, a space after it is not read.
notes.5: Bug: a shape without fields gives `array<never, never>`, the empty array, although `...` makes it open, as the documentation describes.
notes.6: Not implemented: `...<>` takes a key type and a value type, a single one is an open request, psalm#13774.
notes.7: By design: the keys of a list shape have to run from `0` in order, a dedicated error says so.
notes.8: Bug: a shape without fields gives `array<never, never>`, the empty array, although `...` makes it open.
notes.9: Not implemented: no shape after `non-empty-array`, an open request, psalm#13774.
notes.10: Not implemented: `...` is read only in array and list shapes.
notes.11: Not implemented: the key of an object shape is a name or a quoted string only.
notes.12: Not implemented: a shape is read only after `array`, `list`, `non-empty-array`, `non-empty-list` and `object`.
notes.13: Not implemented: a shape is read only after `array`, `list`, `object` and `callable-array`.
notes.14: Bug: the shapes of a union are merged into `array{a?: int, b?: string}`, which also admits `[]` and an array with both keys. A maintainer knows no reason for it, psalm#5212, the fix is open, psalm#10002.
notes.15: By design: a duplicate key is rejected while parsing.
